title: Middle Pleistocene green Sahara episodes
summary: Over the Middle Pleistocene the Sahara repeatedly turned wetter, with grassland, lakes and rivers spreading across what is now desert. Orbital changes in sunshine strengthened the African monsoon in step with the precession cycle, and large ice sheets during glacial periods suppressed many of these humid episodes.

uncertainty.note: The start is the 800,000-year window of the model study; the end is where the Eemian green Sahara (122–128 kyr BP) begins. Individual episodes are spaced by the precession cycle; none is dated individually here.

as_recorded.calendar: Years before present (kyr BP), model with proxy comparison

importance.justification: Repeated humid phases opened the Sahara as habitat and a plausible corridor for plants, animals and hominins.

reviewer_note: The id carries -330ka, but neither paper dates an episode at 330 ka, so no single date is claimed; the range is the 800,000-year model window up to the Eemian. I did not source the formal boundaries of the Middle Pleistocene. The Murzuq Basin is named only in a reference title in Armstrong et al., not a data result I read. Needs a full review for episode-level dates.
